steps.title: AO3 Weighting
steps.body: Context is worth 15-25% of marks. Always link context to specific analysis, never just list facts.

steps.title: Caution
steps.body: Don't reduce poems to autobiography. Use biography to illuminate, not define meaning.

steps.title: Never bolt context on
steps.body: "This poem was written in 1917 during WW1. Owen shows..." Integrate context: "Owen's graphic imagery of 'gargling blood' reflects the brutal reality of trench warfare, challenging the patriotic lies told to families at home."

steps.title: Top Tip
steps.body: AO3 (context) is worth 15-25% of poetry marks depending on your exam board. Context must be integrated into your analysis — never bolt it on as a separate paragraph. Every context point should be linked to a specific quotation or technique. A single well-integrated context point outperforms three disconnected facts.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What is the difference between historical context and biographical context? | Why were Romantic poets interested in nature? | How does World War I context affect war poetry?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Historical context = the time period, events, social conditions when written. Biographical context = the poet's personal life, experiences, background. Both shape the poem but in different ways. | Romantic poets wrote during the Industrial Revolution, which threatened rural life and nature. They saw nature as spiritual, pure, and worth preserving against industrial destruction. | WWI was the first industrialised mass war. Poets like Owen wrote from trenches, challenging glorification.
